# A GNOME Shell surface can pass every adapter test and still get no ref

## Problem

The shell surfaces (tray, notifications, quick settings) are built from virtual nodes and shell widgets. Four of their properties differ from an application's. Each one broke the end-to-end path while the adapter's own tests stayed green (`probes/linux/FINDINGS.md` L32-34, L32-35, L32-28, L32-37).

## What was true

1. **Core drops an entry whose identifier kind is `Unknown`.** `validate_ref_entry` rejects it, and allocation returns `SkippedInvalidEntry` with no error. A platform node without a native id must carry a typed kind. The tray uses `RuntimeId` (`crates/linux/src/system/tray/node_evidence.rs:20-28`), which passes the gate at `crates/core/src/refs/refs_validate.rs:38-45`. Hand-built `RefEntry` values in adapter tests never reach this gate, so only the CLI's `ref_count` shows the drop.
2. **Shell landmarks sit several levels below the container you expect.** The tray panel is two levels above the `System` menu button. The direct children of the panel are nameless groups, and the item buttons are `menu` nodes under them. A lookup by direct child finds nothing, so every item reads as offscreen and unbound (L32-35). The tray no longer binds items to panel nodes. A tray node carries no bounds of its own and an unknown offscreen state (`crates/linux/src/system/tray/live.rs:21-61`).
3. **The shell emits notification signals from its own unique name.** A monitor filtered on the destination `org.freedesktop.Notifications` sees none of them. Match on the interface instead, as `scripts/notification-oracle.sh` does with `dbus-monitor`. The daemon keeps no replay, so a rule added after the click receives nothing (L32-15).
4. **The tray popup is not an application menu surface.** A headed click on an item opens the shell's popup, but the shell tree has no popup node and `list-surfaces` lists none. Its entries are virtual children of the item, read through dbusmenu and picked with `Event(id, "clicked")` (L32-36, L32-37). Do not wait for a `menu` surface after a tray click.

## Prevention

- Check a new virtual node against core's gates by reading `ref_count` and `ref_id` from the CLI's JSON, not by building the entry in a test.
- Measure a lookup's depth against the real shell tree before you rely on direct children.
- Pick the D-Bus oracle by the sender's unique name, and subscribe before the action.
- Read a shell popup through its data source, never through a surface the shell does not expose.

# AgentDeskFixture (Windows)

A WinForms application built and controlled by the Windows live E2E harness
(`tests/e2e-windows/`). It exists so the harness can drive the real
`agent-desktop.exe` binary against a real window and verify every effect by
independent re-observation of the fixture, rather than by the command's own
`ok:true`.

## Build

```powershell
.\build.ps1 [-OutputDir <path>]
```

`csc.exe` is resolved by absolute path
(`%WINDIR%\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe`), never through
`PATH`, so the build cannot silently pick up a different in-box compiler.
`-OutputDir` defaults to a `build` directory next to this script, which is
where `tests/e2e-windows/Run-E2E.ps1` looks for `AgentDeskFixture.exe` unless
it is given `-FixtureBinary`.

The build is idempotent: it compiles to a temporary file and only replaces
the previous `AgentDeskFixture.exe` once the compile has fully succeeded.

## Toolchain constraint: C# 5 only

The in-box compiler at that path (`csc.exe`, version `4.8.3761.0`,
"NET48REL1" on the measured box, A24-1) is the legacy pre-Roslyn .NET
Framework compiler. It accepts `/langversion:5` at most; `6` and above fail
with `CS1617`. Every `.cs` file in this directory
must therefore avoid string interpolation, expression-bodied members,
`nameof`, and null-conditional operators. None of those constructs compile
under this toolchain, regardless of `/langversion`.

## Identity

Every interactive control's `AutomationId` comes from WinForms
`Control.Name`, assigned through `FixtureIdentity.Assign` rather than set
directly, so every control the fixture creates is accounted for. No
`.exe.config` is shipped or required: `Control.Name` surfaces as UIA
`AutomationId` on this toolchain with no `Switch.UseLegacyAccessibilityFeatures`
override needed.

`FixtureIdentity.WriteManifest` writes every id assigned so far, deduplicated
and sorted, to `AgentDeskFixture.ids.txt` beside the running exe on every
launch. The Preconditions scenario of the harness diffs this file against
`tests/e2e-windows/fixture-inventory.psd1` as a set-equality check in both
directions, so a control removed from the fixture without a matching removal
from the inventory (or vice versa) fails the run instead of silently
shrinking coverage.

`WriteManifest` runs exactly once, from `Main`, immediately after the main
form's constructor returns. Every identity-bearing control must therefore be
**constructed** (and so `Assign`ed) by that point, even if it is not yet
**shown**. A control whose construction is deferred until a later user
action (a lazily-built modal dialog, a context menu's items, a duplicate
window opened on demand) will be missing from the manifest, even though it
carries a real, working `AutomationId` once it exists. Build every card's
controls eagerly in the form's own constructor and reveal them later,
rather than constructing them on demand.

## Status readouts

`FixtureStatus` is the one primitive every later effect assertion rests on:
a read-only `TextBox` (`ControlType.Edit`, carrying `ValuePattern`) whose
`AutomationId` is its identity and whose live `.Text` is its value. The two
are separate slots, so a value change can never be mistaken for an identity
change. Every status starts at the sentinel `idle`; every write through
`FixtureStatus.SetValue` appends a monotonically increasing per-status
counter to the assigned value. No two writes to the same status ever produce
the same text, so no leg can pass on a value an earlier leg left behind.

Read a status through `agent-desktop get --property value`, never through
`--property text` or `--property name`. `value` is the property a
`ValuePattern`-bearing `Edit` answers and a `Label` cannot. That difference
lets the read itself tell a correct implementation apart from the one-slot
`Label` shape it must not regress to.

Not every `TextBox` readout goes through `FixtureStatus.SetValue`'s counter.
Two kinds exist, and a scenario author has to know which is which before
writing an equality assertion against one:

- **Counter-suffixed markers** (`click-status`, `text-status`, `menu-status`,
  every other `*-status` id): an opaque, monotonically-numbered marker
  (`"clicked#1"`, `"changed#2"`) that proves *an* effect landed, never the
  literal content of the action. A leg asserts "changed from what it was
  before", never a specific string.
- **Literal-value readouts** (`delayed-text`, `appeared-text`,
  `scroll-offset`): built through `FixtureStatus.Create` for the identity
  shape but written to directly (`.Text = "ready"`), bypassing the counter,
  because the exact string *is* the thing under test. The auto-wait leg
  polls `delayed-text` for the literal value `ready`, not for "any value
  different from before".

## Non-Control identity does not surface as AutomationId

`Control.Name` surfaces as UIA `AutomationId` with no `.exe.config` (A24-2),
but that is a property of `Control`, not of every WinForms item type.
Measured live against a running build of this fixture (`agent-desktop find
--native-id <id>`, zero matches in every case below):

- **`ToolStripItem.Name` does not surface as `AutomationId`.** A
  `ToolStripSplitButton` carrying a `Name` for `menu-disclosure` and a
  top-level `ToolStripMenuItem` carrying a `Name` for `menu-fire-item` were
  both unresolvable by `--native-id`, even though the *container*
  `ToolStrip`/`MenuStrip` (a real `Control`) resolved fine.
- **`TreeNode.Name` does not surface as `AutomationId`** either, for the same
  reason: a `TreeNode` is not a `Control`. A stock `TreeView`'s own
  `AutomationId` (a real `Control`) resolved fine; its child nodes did not.

Every target that needs to resolve by native id and needed a `ControlType`
no stock control produces is instead a real `Control` (a `Button`, `Label` or
`Panel`) wearing a `WM_GETOBJECT` override provider (`UiaProviderHost` and its
subclasses in `FixtureProviderHost.cs`, `FixtureToggleHost.cs`,
`FixtureExpandCollapseHost.cs` and `FixtureControlTypeOverrideHost.cs`):
`menu-disclosure`, `menu-fire-item`, `outline-tree`,
`outline-parent`, `outline-child-a`, `outline-child-b`, `cell-griditem`,
`cell-custom`, `row-plain`. `outline-tree` is
therefore not a real `System.Windows.Forms.TreeView`: it is a `Panel`
holding three `Label`s arranged with indentation, each independently
overriding its own `ControlType`.

A registered custom raw provider also does **not** transparently inherit
the host's `InvokePattern` availability the way bounds/enabled/offscreen
merge through `HostRawElementProvider`. Measured live against
`menu-fire-item` with no explicit `IInvokeProvider`, `InvokePattern.Invoke`
came back `skipped`, and the click chain's `LegacyIAccessible.DoDefaultAction`
fallback reported success without the Click handler ever running.
`ControlTypeOverrideHost` therefore takes an optional invoke callback and implements `IInvokeProvider` itself
whenever a wrapped target must stay clickable through the CLI.

## Non-activating launch

Set `AGENT_DESKTOP_FIXTURE_NO_ACTIVATE=1` in the launching environment to
have the main window shown via `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` instead of stealing the
foreground; `Run-E2E.ps1` sets it. Unset (or any value other than `1`), the
window activates normally.

## Process lifetime

`Main()` calls `Application.Run(form)` with the main `AgentDeskFixture`
instance rather than the parameterless overload, so the message loop and the
process exit when that specific form closes, regardless of how many
secondary windows (duplicate-title targets, modal dialogs, overlays) happen
to be open at the time.

# Test Fixtures

Hand-written golden files that tests compare serialized output against. None is captured from a real app.

| Fixture | Asserted by |
|---|---|
| `skeleton-tree.json` | `test_skeleton_fixture_matches_golden` in `crates/core/src/snapshot/snapshot_tests.rs` |
| `drilldown-refmap.json` | `test_drilldown_refmap_matches_golden_fixture` in `crates/core/src/snapshot/snapshot_ref_merge_tests.rs` |
| `trace_show/trace/*.jsonl` | `show_merges_fixture_segments_with_expected_shape` in `crates/core/src/commands/trace_tests.rs` |

The JSON fixtures are loaded at compile time, so a missing or renamed file breaks the build:

```rust
let golden = include_str!("../../../../tests/fixtures/skeleton-tree.json");
```

Any change to the shape a fixture pins must update the fixture in the same commit.

#Requires -Version 5.1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Invert-verified self-test for run-windows-e2e-ci.ps1's refusal guard
    (U14 invert item 20): with AGENT_DESKTOP_NATIVE_E2E_RUNNER unset,
    run-windows-e2e-ci.ps1 must exit 2 having touched neither the staged
    release binary nor started any product or fixture process.

.DESCRIPTION
    "Asserted by the absence of the build output" is not usable: on any
    machine that has already run `cargo build --release`, the binary
    already exists, so that predicate is vacuously true whether or not the
    guard actually fired. This self-test instead requires the binary to
    already exist (a prior CI step builds it) and asserts its
    LastWriteTime is byte-for-byte unchanged across the invocation, plus a
    pid snapshot before/after proving no new agent-desktop.exe or
    AgentDeskFixture.exe process was started. Run on the hosted
    windows-latest lane, never against a real desktop lease.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param()

Set-StrictMode -Version 2.0
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$repoRoot = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSCommandPath))
$binaryPath = Join-Path $repoRoot 'target\release\agent-desktop.exe'
$runScript = Join-Path $repoRoot 'scripts\run-windows-e2e-ci.ps1'

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $binaryPath)) {
    throw "run-windows-e2e-ci-refusal-selftest: $binaryPath must already exist (build the release binary first) - an absent binary would make the unchanged-mtime predicate vacuously true"
}

$beforeWrite = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $binaryPath).LastWriteTimeUtc
$beforePids = @(Get-Process -Name 'agent-desktop', 'AgentDeskFixture' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Id)

Remove-Item Env:AGENT_DESKTOP_NATIVE_E2E_RUNNER -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
& powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $runScript
$exitCode = $LASTEXITCODE

$afterWrite = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $binaryPath).LastWriteTimeUtc
$afterPids = @(Get-Process -Name 'agent-desktop', 'AgentDeskFixture' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Id)
$newPids = @($afterPids | Where-Object { $beforePids -notcontains $_ })

$failed = 0
if ($exitCode -ne 2) {
    Write-Host "FAIL: run-windows-e2e-ci.ps1 exited $exitCode without AGENT_DESKTOP_NATIVE_E2E_RUNNER set; expected 2"
    $failed = 1
}
if ($afterWrite -ne $beforeWrite) {
    Write-Host "FAIL: $binaryPath's last-write time changed ($beforeWrite -> $afterWrite) - the refusal guard let a build proceed"
    $failed = 1
}
if ($newPids.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "FAIL: new agent-desktop/AgentDeskFixture process(es) appeared during the refusal invocation: $($newPids -join ', ')"
    $failed = 1
}

if ($failed -ne 0) { exit 1 }

# Locator resolution benchmark

This deterministic harness compares the legacy full-snapshot locator path with
the handle-free observed-tree evaluator over synthetic Chromium/Electron accessibility
trees. It exercises deep anonymous wrapper chains, duplicate role/name
candidates, moving bounds, simultaneous `AXIdentifier` and `AXDOMIdentifier`
values, containment predicates, and large trees.

Run it without network access:

```bash
cargo run -p agent-desktop-core --release --example locator_benchmark \
  > /tmp/agent-desktop-locator-synthetic.json
```

The JSON report includes 31-run p50/p95 wall-clock latency, candidate nodes,
predicate work, requested synthetic attribute values, cardinality, and
correctness. `live_find_selected_refs` uses the same selected-match-only
materialization contract as the default CLI `find` path. `live_arena_direct` is
reported separately as a lower-overhead direct-target metric, and
`live_count_no_refmap` verifies that count-only requests perform no action or
settable evidence reads. The harness does not claim absolute native AX calls:
role-dependent action and settable probes make that model inaccurate. Native
Slack/Electron IPC measurements require Accessibility permission and belong in
the privileged macOS integration suite.

This synthetic benchmark JSON is consumed by the repo-wide performance report:
run `bash scripts/perf-baseline-compare.sh` (optionally with `--apps "Slack,Google
Chrome"`) to produce `report.html`, covering the HEAD-vs-main fixture A/B,
optional real-app read-only probes, and this synthetic benchmark.

For privileged Electron/Chromium runs, the macOS adapter first asks whether the
application root exposes `AXManualAccessibility` as settable, reads its current
value, and sets it at most once when supported. The adapter then waits within
the request's existing absolute deadline until the attribute reports ready,
recording attempted/succeeded/ready activation in locator stats. Unsupported
native applications are left unchanged. This follows
[Electron's official third-party accessibility guidance](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/tutorial/accessibility.md),
which documents setting `AXManualAccessibility` from native assistive software
to expose Chromium's accessibility tree before automatic assistive-technology
detection has enabled it. The
[current Electron macOS implementation](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/mac/electron_application.mm)
advertises the attribute as settable, reports `true` only in complete mode, and
handles `AXEnhancedUserInterface` separately; that source behavior is why the
benchmark methodology requires a post-set readiness read instead of treating a
successful setter as immediate readiness.

# Adapter Reliability Conformance

Every platform adapter must satisfy the same ref/action contract. The tests are
written against `PlatformAdapter` semantics, so macOS AX, Windows UIA and Linux
AT-SPI share the same expectations.

The reusable command-path helper lives in `tests/conformance/ref_action_contract.rs`.
`window_identity_contract.rs` holds the window-identity contract, and
`macos_notification_contract.rs` the macOS-only notification contract. The
executable smoke harness in `src/tests/conformance.rs` mounts all three and runs
the ref/action helper against a mock adapter. A fixture driving a real adapter
can call the same helper with adapter-provided refs.

## Required Gates

| Area | Required behavior |
|------|-------------------|
| Snapshot refs | Refs are depth-first, snapshot-qualified (`@<snapshot_id>:eN`), and a bare `@eN` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS` |
| Strict resolve | A ref resolves only when identity still matches; stale refs return `STALE_REF` |
| Ambiguity | Multiple plausible matches return `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`, never an arbitrary click |
| Actionability | Ref actions check live visibility, stability, enabled state, supported action, policy, and editability before dispatch |
| Wait recovery | `wait --element` polls the snapshot embedded in its qualified ref, honors the caller timeout while resolving, and reports the last observed predicate state |
| Snapshot scope | A qualified ref resolves its own snapshot inside the selected session namespace and never searches other sessions |
| Trace | With a `trace: on` session manifest (from `session start`), commands write per-process JSONL segments under the session directory. `--trace <path>` overrides to one file. Best-effort unless `--trace-strict`. |
| Session lifecycle | `session start/end/list/gc` manage manifests, the current-session pointer, and trace directories |
| FFI parity | FFI ref actions use strict resolve and actionability checks before adapter dispatch |

## Platform Matrix

| Fixture | macOS AX | Windows UIA | Linux AT-SPI |
|---------|:--------:|:-----------:|:------------:|
| Two identical buttons produce ambiguity | Required | Required | Required |
| Ref disappears after snapshot | Required | Required | Required |
| Disabled button blocks click before dispatch | Required | Required | Required |
| Text field supports value/type actionability | Required | Required | Required |
| Session A latest refmap is invisible to Session B | Required | Required | Required |
| Batch item session overrides inherited session | Required | Required | Required |
| FFI `AdRefEntry` preserves full identity envelope | Required | Required | Required |

## Adding a Platform

Add adapter-specific integration fixtures, but keep expected errors and JSON
shapes identical. Prefer semantic platform actions first (`AXPress`, UIA
Invoke/Value/Selection patterns, AT-SPI actions). Coordinate input is a lower
confidence fallback and must remain explicit in policy or command choice.

## Windows Private-Storage Gate

Windows private-file behavior is verified by native tests, never by
cross-compilation evidence alone. The Windows CI lanes run these suites natively:

| Behavior | Native test |
|----------|-------------|
| A junction as a path component, the parent, or the leaf is refused and nothing lands at its target | `crates/windows/src/system/private_file/path_tests.rs` |
| A validated ancestor cannot be renamed while the write holds its no-follow handle | `a_pinned_directory_cannot_be_renamed_while_its_no_follow_handle_is_held` in `path_tests.rs` |
| A foreign owner is refused on atomic write, append, and bounded read | `owner_tests.rs` |
| A fresh artifact keeps its inherited SYSTEM, Administrators, and user grants, and never `BUILTIN\Users`, across create and replace | `a_profile_artifact_keeps_system_admins_and_user_and_never_users_across_create_and_replace` in `owner_tests.rs` |
| Remote or undeterminable storage refuses the write and append surfaces | `locality_tests.rs` |
| Atomic replace succeeds over open readers and concurrent writers, and leaves no temporary residue | `replace_tests.rs` |
| The binary and the FFI adapter install the hardened seam, and `session start` through a junction state root is refused with nothing written under the target | `src/tests/windows_private_file_install.rs`, `crates/ffi/tests/c_abi_windows_private_file_install.rs` |

The module protects each private directory it creates with a protected DACL
(`dacl::protect_directory`) granting SYSTEM, Administrators, the token user and
the owner-eligible SIDs, and `dacl::require_private` checks that DACL before use.
Files created in such a directory inherit those grants, which
`a_profile_artifact_keeps_system_admins_and_user_and_never_users_across_create_and_replace`
in `owner_tests.rs` pins.

# Linux live end-to-end harness

Drives the built `agent-desktop` binary against real GNOME and Qt applications inside private, throwaway desktop sessions. Every effect is verified by an independent read (raw AT-SPI, X11, GSettings, process, pixel, clipboard or D-Bus), never by the command's own `ok:true`.

## Run

Build the CLI and its adjacent clipboard owner and run one tier in one call:

```sh
bash tests/e2e-linux/run.sh --tier x11-openbox
```

Each run builds (`cargo build --locked --release`) into its own suite's temporary Cargo target, stages both executables in `<suite>/bin/`, and records their SHA256s in adjacent `.sha256` files and in the startup `image:` lines. It then removes the build intermediates. Every leg uses that pinned pair. A staged hash mismatch fails the run, and other worktrees' builds cannot replace either image. An externally supplied `AGENT_DESKTOP_E2E_BIN` (or `AGENT_DESKTOP_E2E_BIN_SRC`) skips the build and freezes that image and its adjacent helper before the interaction lease is taken.

Omit `--tier` to run all tiers sequentially. Set `AGENT_DESKTOP_E2E_SUITE` to a fresh directory to choose the evidence location. The default is a fresh directory under `$AGENT_DESKTOP_SESSION_BASE` when nonempty, otherwise `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/agent-desktop-sessions` when `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is nonempty, otherwise `/tmp/agent-desktop-sessions-<uid>` with the numeric user ID. The base is created with mode 0700. The runner starts its own private sessions and takes the interaction lease.

Exit codes: `0` every leg passed or asserted its refusal; `1` any other outcome (see Outcomes); `2` the gate refused to start (missing prerequisite, unknown leg, leg not registered for the tier, staging failure, or the interaction lease is already held). Nothing ran on exit 2.

Keep failed suites for diagnosis; the runner removes a successful suite. Use another fresh suite for the sole diagnostic rerun. Do not reuse a suite with a different binary image.

### Prerequisites

`runner/gate.py` is the authoritative list; a missing item exits 2 before any leg runs.

- Python 3 with PyGObject (`import gi`).
- Base tools: `Xvfb`, `dbus-daemon`, `dbus-update-activation-environment`, `gdbus`, `busctl`, `gsettings`, `setsid`, `xprop`, `xwininfo`, `xwd`, `fusermount`, `timeout`.
- `x11-openbox`: `xdotool`, `wmctrl`, `xclip`, and the openbox binary at `$AGENT_DESKTOP_WM_ROOT/usr/bin/openbox` (`AGENT_DESKTOP_WM_ROOT` defaults to `/`).
- `x11-mutter`: `gnome-shell`, `xdotool`, `wmctrl`, `xclip`.
- `wayland`: `gnome-shell`, `wl-copy`, `wl-paste`.
- The legs also drive the GNOME apps Calculator, Text Editor, Files, Terminal and Settings, and a PyQt6 test window. AT-SPI must be available in the private session.

The runner inherits the caller's tool paths and libraries: supply tools through `PATH` and shared libraries through `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Qt legs run under `python3`; set `AGENT_DESKTOP_QT_PYTHON` when PyQt6 lives in a separate interpreter. That does not change the harness interpreter.

## Tiers

- `--tier x11-openbox`: private Xvfb and openbox.
- `--tier x11-mutter`: private Xvfb and the private mutter shell wrapper.
- `--tier wayland`: private bus and a health-gated headless GNOME Wayland shell.

Each tier runs the headless and headed modes registered for that leg. A headed mode on a headless compositor sends synthetic input inside that private session, not to the user's desktop.

`events.open_and_close_inside_one_wait` and `ref_actions.drag` are registered on openbox only. On Mutter, the first leg tore down against a vanished AT-SPI node. The second timed out during editor registry setup before it dispatched a product command. Neither counts as a Mutter pass. A leg that is not registered for a tier makes no live claim there.

## Legs

Use `--leg <id>` with the same tier to reproduce a single registered leg:

```sh
bash tests/e2e-linux/run.sh --tier x11-openbox --leg clipboard.text_roundtrip
```

`runner/legs.py` is the inventory of IDs, tiers, modes, oracles and dispositions. Pass `--leg id1,id2,id3` to run a bounded batch in one private tier session. Every requested ID must be registered for the selected tier; a mismatch exits 2. A single ID executes all its registered modes; it is not a mode selector.

A pass requires independent before/after observations, restoration where state changed, and the same attributed app process generations after cleanup. A refusal leg must assert its expected error and absence of effect.

Per-leg cleanup stops each attributed app generation. Private background services may start or exit independently; their membership does not show an app leak. Private-session teardown sweeps all runtime members and fails if any survive.

To list registered IDs, modes and dispositions for a tier without starting apps:

```sh
python3 -I - <<'PYLIST'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "tests/e2e-linux")
from runner.legs import REGISTRY
for leg in REGISTRY:
    if "x11-openbox" in leg.tiers:
        print(leg.id, ",".join(leg.modes), leg.disposition, leg.reason)
PYLIST
```

Change the tier string to `x11-mutter` or `wayland` for those inventories.

### Outcomes

The report groups outcomes by tier and mode. Only `pass` and `asserted-refusal` exit 0.

| Outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pass` | Every before, after and restored read agreed and the owned process set was unchanged. |
| `asserted-refusal` | The leg's expected result is the product's refusal with a named error code and no effect; it was observed. |
| `fail` | An assertion failed, an oracle read was missing or out of order, state drifted and was not restored, or the owned process set changed. |
| `error` | An unexpected exception, an evidence write failure, a changed staged binary, or a teardown failure. |
| `blocked` | The leg raised `NotImplementedError`. |
| `unimplemented` | The leg is registered but has no implementation. |
| `outstanding`, `owner-decision` | Registered but deliberately not run; the reason is printed. |
| `tier-unavailable` | The tier's private session never became healthy or its desktop warm-up failed, so its legs did not run. |

The `launch.recovery_strategy_on_error` leg is an `asserted-refusal`. It stops Calculator after a snapshot, then requires a click on the dead owner's ref to answer `STALE_REF` with `details.process_state=exited`, `details.retryable=false` and disposition `not_delivered`/`safe`, with no `recovery` object and no relaunch of the owner.

The `error_contract.recoverable_error_envelopes` leg is an `asserted-refusal` on both X11 tiers. Against a live Calculator it requires a bare `@e1` to answer `INVALID_ARGS` with the snapshot-qualified suggestion, `@sdeadbeef:e1` to answer `SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND` with the `refresh_snapshot_then_retry_original` recovery, and an unknown `--app` to answer `APP_NOT_FOUND` with the `list-apps` suggestion. Each must be `not_delivered` and exit 1, and the Calculator display and the owned-process set must be unchanged.

The `observation.stale_ref_after_ui_change` leg is an `asserted-refusal` on both X11 tiers. It mints a ref to the Calculator About menu item, closes the menu through the raw toggle, and requires `click` on that ref to answer `STALE_REF` with the `refresh_snapshot_then_retry_original` recovery, `not_delivered` and exit 1 while the app stays owned and the display is unchanged; a fresh snapshot must then mint a different ref.

The `text_entry.press_combos_edit_document` leg runs headed on both X11 tiers: after a semantic `type`, `press return` must add exactly one newline to the AT-SPI document text, `press ctrl+a` then `press backspace` must empty it, and no X11 modifier may stay down. A headless `press` is refused by the physical-input policy before any key is sent, so only the headed run proves delivery.

The `batch_contract.entry_failure_and_stop_on_error` leg is an `asserted-refusal` on both X11 tiers. A three-entry batch (click 7, click an absent ref, click 8) must report `STALE_REF` on entry 1 inside an `ok` batch envelope and still run entry 2, leaving `78` on the Calculator display. The same batch with `--stop-on-error` must report `stopped` as `stop_on_error` at index 1 with two completed entries and one not started, leaving `7`. The display is read through AT-SPI, not the envelope, and Undo restores it.

### Ref-action contracts

The `ref_actions.*` legs observe and restore native application state:

| Action | Independent effect |
| --- | --- |
| Focus | Qt Text entry gains `FOCUSED`; the prior button regains it on restoration. |
| Double-click / triple-click | Text Editor selects a word / line, read through AT-SPI Text selection offsets. |
| Right-click | Text Editor exposes a showing `Context menu` and its menu-item children. |
| Hover | The Qt probe's native status tip appears and clears when the pointer leaves. |
| Expand / collapse | Calculator's Main Menu changes `EXPANDED` and showing menu children together. |
| Scroll | Settings Hot Corner leaves the viewport and Dynamic Workspaces enters it. |
| Scroll-to | Settings reveals the offscreen monitor checkbox without changing its checked state. |
| Drag | Text Editor gains a nonempty text selection. |

Headless focus, double-click, triple-click, hover, scroll and drag are separate `asserted-refusal` legs requiring `POLICY_DENIED`, no app effect and unchanged pointer and focus. Right-click, expand/collapse and scroll-to have semantic success legs in both modes. The `pointer.*` legs compare the product's delivery report with an independent read of the app state, in both delivered and undelivered cases. A fabricated report or pointer movement alone cannot pass. The `mouse-click`, `drag` and `mouse-wheel` delivery legs read the actual effect: the Calculator digit, the Text Editor selection or the scrollbar position. Text Editor is seeded in memory through raw `EditableText`, and selection cleanup sends Right only after requiring that the exact owned window is active.

### Notification and tray legs

Notification legs (`notifications.*`) run on `x11-mutter`, where the private GNOME shell owns the notification server; `oracle/notify.py` checks that the server's process belongs to the private runtime directory. A separate sender process posts notifications, and a `dbus-monitor` records the daemon's signals in `notification-signals.log`. A leg passes on the sender's IDs, those signals and the list readback, and closes every owned ID with restoration checked before the next leg.

- Headless `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications` and `notification-action` must answer `POLICY_DENIED`, with no daemon signal and an unchanged list.
- `notifications.dismiss_notification_closes_only_target` is headed. It seeds a target and a bystander, requires a wrong `--expected-app` to answer `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` with no signal and no list change, then requires only the target's daemon close (reason 2), the bystander still active, and a list containing only the bystander.

Tray legs (`tray.*`, `x11-mutter`, headless) register a harness StatusNotifierItem (`apps/sni_item.py`) and read its call log: `Activate`, menu `Event(id, clicked)`, the refusal for an item without `Activate`, and a killed owner turning the old ref into `STALE_REF`.

The registry is the inventory; these surfaces have no live claim, and their coverage lives in the named tests.

- Electron and Chromium: no leg in this registry.
- Clipboard HTML import: unsupported by design. `clipboard-get` reads only the text and image targets (`formats::TEXT_TARGETS`, `targets::choose_target`; `x11_read_tests::an_owner_without_the_wanted_target_reads_as_absent`). ## Reading a failure

The printed report groups every outcome by tier and mode. Failed runs retain `report.txt` and per-leg JSON evidence in the printed suite directory. Evidence includes product argv, response envelopes, oracle reads, and process membership. Read `report.txt` first, then pretty-print the matching `evidence/<tier>/<mode>/<leg-id>.json` with `python3 -m json.tool`. Its `exception_traceback`, `products`, `reads`, and `owned_baseline`/`owned_final` show whether failure occurred before dispatch, at the effect check, or during restoration. A matching deterministic product failure needs the same command, preconditions and independent effect/no-effect reads on the diagnostic rerun. A raw-bus, launch, timing or service-membership failure before product dispatch is a fixture/environment failure; preserve its evidence when retiring it.

Rerun a failed leg at most once to distinguish a deterministic product defect from timing, load, session setup, or environment behavior. Delete an unstable leg or replace it with a deterministic fake or an observed-state wait, and record the reason in a `test:` commit. Fix product code only for a deterministic product defect, especially wrong-target input or false delivery evidence.

`--lying-actions` replaces the CLI with a fake that always answers `ok:true` without real refs or effects, so any selection must fail. ```

### Cancellation check

At startup the runner prints `suite:` and both `image:` hashes. When a private tier's accessibility health gate passes, it atomically publishes `<suite>/<tier>.ready.json` and prints `cancel-ready:` with that path, the runtime directory, `harness-owner` marker, runner PID and Linux `/proc` start token (field 22, ticks since boot). The marker contains `<pid> <start-token>`. The background shell/interaction-lock wrapper PID is not the runner PID.

This bounded check waits for the receipt rather than guessing a PID or sleeping before a signal:

```sh
export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0
base=${AGENT_DESKTOP_SESSION_BASE:-${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:+$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/agent-desktop-sessions}}
base=${base:-/tmp/agent-desktop-sessions-$(id -u)}
umask 077
mkdir -p "$base"
suite=$(mktemp -d "$base/e2e-cancel.XXXXXX")
AGENT_DESKTOP_E2E_SUITE="$suite" bash tests/e2e-linux/run.sh \
  --tier x11-mutter --leg ref_actions.right_click >"$suite/run.log" 2>&1 &
job=$!
python3 -I tests/e2e-linux/runner/cancel.py "$suite/x11-mutter.ready.json" --wait 600
signal_rc=$?
wait "$job"; rc=$?
cat "$suite/run.log"
test "$signal_rc" -eq 0 && test "$rc" -eq 143 || exit 1
python3 -I tests/e2e-linux/runner/cancel.py "$suite/x11-mutter.ready.json" \
  --check-cleanup --wait 60
```

`cancel.py` checks the marker, exact `runner/main.py` command, user and start token before sending SIGTERM through a Linux PID descriptor. A changed or exited generation is refused. The final check waits until the runtime directory is absent and no process environment references it. Run these commands together in one local shell. The next run sweeps abandoned sessions whose recorded runner has exited.

| 2 | Every `ad_*_size()` getter equals the corresponding `AD_*_SIZE` macro (catches struct layout drift) |

## Building the dylib

```bash
# From the repo root:
cargo build --locked --profile release-ffi -p agent-desktop-ffi --features stub-adapter
```

returns `PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED` for every adapter call. This lets CI run the

# A cited measurement must match its capture

## Problem

Probe row `A21-6` recorded that an uncontended `SetForegroundWindow` lands on the first attempt every time. The capture it names, committed beside the row, recorded the opposite: the first attempt did not take ownership, and a second attempt was needed.

The false sentence propagated. A design document that sized the retry budget repeated it, and a doc comment on the shipped constant cited the row id. The product's own source claimed a measurement its evidence contradicted. No gate failed, because no gate compared a row's prose to the JSON it names.

## Root cause

The row was written from the expectation that motivated the probe, not from the artifact. The design did not depend on the answer, since a retry budget of two is correct either way, so the wrong number changed no behaviour and drew no attention. Downstream readers cite the row rather than the capture. That makes the row a single point of failure that nobody re-derives.

## Solution

Correct the row against the capture, and correct every site that repeated it, in the same change. Keep the design when the evidence still supports it: a first-attempt rate of zero supports a bounded retry more strongly than a perfect rate would.

Check a row by reading the fields it names, not the fields you expected the capture to have:

```bash
python -c "import json,io; d=json.load(io.open('<capture>.json',encoding='utf-8-sig')); print(d)"
```

Two properties make a row auditable:

- Quote the field names and values the capture uses. A row that says `first_attempt_success_rate: 0` can be diffed against the JSON. A row that says "the first attempt is reliable" cannot.
- Record the verdict the probe wrote (`branch`, `measurable`) rather than paraphrasing it.

## Prevention

- Write the row from the capture open beside you, never from the question the probe was written to answer. A row written without re-reading its capture is unverified.
- When a finding is the answer the author hoped for, re-read the capture once more. Confirming results get less scrutiny than contradicting ones, which is backwards.
- Open the capture before citing a row in shipped source or a design document. Repeating a row is not evidence that it is true.
- When correcting a row, correct every downstream repetition in the same change.
- A design that is right for a reason the evidence does not support is still undefended. Fix the sentence even when the code stays.
- The binary a probe measured must be the binary the product runs. A probe that measures an absolute path does not cover a call made by bare name, and a test helper must use the same resolution as the product. On Windows, a bare `tar` resolved to GNU tar from Git for Windows, which read drive-letter archive paths as network hosts.
- Repetition fixes noise, not environment. Min-of-N gives a stable number for the machine it ran on. A single unrepeated timed sample is not evidence. A timing claim also has to hold on a second environment, such as a CI runner, before it is written down as fact.
- Report the distribution, not the best case. A minimum answers "how fast can this go", not "what will this cost". Report the median beside it, and the max when the spread is wide.
- The ledger gate `probes/windows/13-ledger-check.ps1` (helpers in `probes/windows/13-ledger-content.ps1`, run by `.github/workflows/windows-capability-probe.yml`) fails a row whose quoted `field: value` pair or counted number disagrees with its capture. A qualitative claim is outside its reach, so the rules above still bind the author.

# Guard OS-reordered resources with an identity fingerprint

## Context

An OS-managed resource can be inserted, removed, recycled, or reassigned
between the moment a caller observes it and the moment an action mutates it.
Notification Center can insert, remove, regroup, or reorder entries between a
list call and a mutation. Windows can destroy a window and hand its `HWND` to
an unrelated process before the next call that uses it. An index or a handle
alone is not an identity: either can end up addressing a different resource
by the time it is used, and wherever the check and the act cannot be issued
as one atomic operation, the gap between them is where the target can change.

## Guidance

**Notification identity.** Notification mutation commands require at least
one identity field from the same list result: expected app or expected
title. Core constructs this with
`commands::notification_identity::required_identity`; an empty identity is
`INVALID_ARGS`. The macOS adapter checks the live entry against
`NotificationIdentity` immediately before it acts and fails closed on
mismatch. FFI follows the same rule: invalid or missing identity data is
rejected instead of being coerced into an unconstrained action, and callers
recover by listing again and selecting a fresh entry.

**Window-handle identity.** A Windows `HWND` is a recyclable handle: once a
window is destroyed, the OS is free to hand the same numeric value to an
unrelated process's next window. Verifying identity once, at entry, is not
enough when the write that follows is not atomic with that check. A handle
can be destroyed and recycled in the gap between the check and the native
write. `focus_window` (`crates/windows/src/system/window/window_activate.rs`)
re-verifies handle ownership (`owned_for_write`) immediately before every
native write that follows entry verification. `restore_if_iconic` re-checks
ownership before its `ShowWindow` call, and `bring_to_foreground` re-checks
before `ShowWindow` / `SetForegroundWindow`. A recycle caught by either of those internal checks
fails closed as `WINDOW_NOT_FOUND` / not-delivered, never a foreground write
to a foreign window.

Re-verifying the precondition before each write is necessary but not
sufficient on its own: the success check has to be identity-qualified too,
or a recycle that wins the race between the last write and the result check
reports success over the wrong window. `is_owned_foreground` requires both
`is_foreground_window(handle)` **and** `evidence.owns_handle_now()`. The
second check confirms that the handle's live owner is still the stored pid
and that pid is still the stored process instance. Handle equality alone is
not enough, because it would accept a recycled HWND
that happens to be foreground for an unrelated reason. See `focus_window`'s own
doc comment in `window_activate.rs` for the stated rationale.

**Display identity.** A Windows display id is a recyclable
`monitor-{HMONITOR}` handle: the same numeric value can later name a
different monitor after hot-plug, mode change, or OS reassignment. Trusting
the id alone between `list-displays` and `screenshot` is the same
check-then-act gap as a bare HWND. Callers pass the full `DisplayInfo` from
the list result; the adapter re-lists and corroborates id together with
bounds, primary, and scale before capture (`verify_display_identity` in
`display.rs`), then verifies again after capture so a mid-capture change
discards the bytes rather than attributing them to the wrong surface
(identity sandwich in `screenshot.rs`). Exact-window screenshot requires a
`process_instance` token for the same reason: HWND alone is not enough.
Backend choice (Modern vs Legacy) is orthogonal: the fingerprint applies
regardless of which capture path produces the PNG.

**Element identity inside repeated collections.** A repeated native identifier does not identify a row. After a filter, a different row can take the original position with the same identifier and bounds, and disabling the path optimization does not help, because a broad search still matches them. Do not freeze mutable values to fix this, since ordinary text inputs must stay editable through the same ref. Without the opt-in internal command host (`AGENT_DESKTOP_INTERNAL_COMMAND_HOST=1`, `src/command_host/mod.rs`), no retained-object token is recorded, so `ref_identity::identity_match` in `crates/core/src/refs/ref_identity.rs` returns `Match` on the shared identifier and the aliasing stays reachable in the default CLI.

## Prevention

- Never expose a mutating list-index or bare-handle API without an identity
  precondition.
- Prefer a stable opaque handle when the platform supplies one; otherwise use
  the smallest reliable fingerprint and verify immediately before mutation.
- When the check and the act cannot be made atomic, a precondition verified
  once at entry is not enough: re-verify identity immediately before *every*
  native write the action performs, not only the first.
- Fold identity into the success predicate itself, not only the
  precondition. A success check built from handle equality alone
  (`GetForegroundWindow() == handle`) cannot tell a genuine success from a
  recycled handle that happens to satisfy it; the check must also confirm
  the resource is still the one the action targeted, not merely that
  something answered at the expected address.
- Test insertion, removal, and title/app mismatch between list and act; for
  a recyclable handle, test the destroy-and-recycle race directly against
  both the precondition and the success predicate.
- For display capture, test each fingerprint field independently (id, bounds,
  primary, scale) mutating between list and act, and assert a post-capture
  mismatch discards the buffer.
- For a repeated native identifier, test an identical replacement at the same
  bounds, and check that normal text editing on an unchanged item still works
  through its ref.

# Native command reliability: scrolling, selection and menu discovery

Trials in this area are bounded to a few apps and runs. They do not establish universal reliability.

## Scroll controls are not identified by their value

A scrollbar's value changes when it scrolls, so the value cannot be stable identity. Core's mutable-value role list omitted `scrollbar` and `handle`. The old value was treated as identity, and a legitimate scroll made the live scrollbar fail to resolve. The fix adds both roles to `is_mutable_value_role` in `crates/core/src/tree/roles.rs`. No timeout, fuzzy match, path trust, or ambiguity rule was relaxed.

Matching values alone remain insufficient identity, and distinct named scroll controls remain distinct. Changed geometry without stable identity still needs a safe refusal. The fix does not promise to recover an arbitrary thumb.

Evidence: `crates/core/src/refs/ref_identity_scroll_tests.rs`, test `scroll_positions_neither_prove_nor_reject_element_identity`.

## Select matches canonical collection labels

`select` searched only AXTitle and AXDescription. Snapshots derive a row's name from its child content, so `select` returned ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND for a row the snapshot had named. The search now reads the same bounded name evidence as snapshots. A candidate must advertise Click, because inert text cannot become an action target just because its text matches. Unknown evidence fails closed, and a missing item reports `not_delivered`.

Menu selection shares this search and has no live regression test yet.

Evidence: `crates/macos/src/actions/select/select_name.rs`, test `selection_requires_a_known_canonical_label_and_an_actionable_target`.

## Incomplete branches cannot prove a menu is absent

The app-wide menu search aborted at the first incomplete branch. In a 6,984-item grid, a branch that loaded only part of its children hid a menu open in a sibling. The search now goes breadth-first and defers `AppUnresponsive` branch errors while it inspects siblings. A menu it observes is returned. Otherwise the incomplete error is kept. Permission errors and deadlines stay terminal, and the 2,048-node limit still applies.

Evidence: `crates/macos/src/tree/surfaces.rs`, test `an_incomplete_branch_cannot_prove_menu_absence`.

## Disclosure controls without readable expansion state

A Weight popup button in SF Symbols published AXShowMenu and AXPress but returned `kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported` for AXExpanded and AXDisclosing. Its expand action refused without delivery. When the expansion state is unknown, test the native menu-opening semantics rather than toggling AXPress blindly.

## Monitored trials need quiet foreground

The headless probe counts session-wide input and observes activation notifications. Activity from the user or other apps appears in those counts, so the events cannot be attributed to the agent. A monitored trial with unrelated foreground activity is not proof of a headless success, and unattributed events earn no credit.

Evidence: `tests/real-apps/headless_probe.swift`, a read-only diagnostic and not a driver.

title: A wait for "closed" right after the opener is satisfied falsely
date: 2026-10-19
category: runtime-errors
module: crates/linux/src/system/interaction/action_clock.rs, crates/linux/src/system/interaction/action_clock_store.rs, crates/linux/src/system/menu/menu_wait.rs
problem_type: runtime_error
component: atspi-menu-wait
symptoms:
  - "wait --menu-closed returns at once after a click that opens a GTK4 popover, before the menu ever showed."
  - "The same sequence passes when click and wait run in one process and fails when they run as two CLI calls."
tags: [linux, at-spi, gtk4, menu, wait, race, persisted-state]
---

## Problem

A GTK4 popover menu appears in the accessibility tree 157 to 331 ms after its opener action returns (L18-2). The live probe saw it open at 540 ms on Calculator and 688 ms on Files (L33-51). A `wait --menu-closed` that starts right after the opener polls a menu that is not yet visible, reads "closed", and returns. The wait is satisfied by the state it was meant to outlast.

## Solution

A closed-direction wait holds until it has seen the menu open, or until 2 s pass since the last action, whichever comes first. `menu_wait.rs` asks `action_clock::recent_for(pid)`; the clock marks every action that started, that is, anything but one refused before it sent (`action_clock::mark_outcome`).

The memory has to outlive the process. An agent runs `click` and `wait` as two CLI calls, so an in-process `Instant` is empty in the second one. `action_clock_store.rs` writes a per-process record under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/agent-desktop-actions`, stamped in milliseconds of boot time (suspend included) so two processes agree and a restart cannot make an old record look new, and keyed by a process-instance token so a reused pid does not inherit it. The first live legs used the in-process clock and passed 10 of 10 (L33-17); only the two-process case (L33-56) exercises the persisted store.

## Prevention

- Test a wait that depends on a prior action in two processes, not one. A unit test with an in-process clock cannot fail for this reason.
- Do not size the hold from one toolkit. The popover delay is measured per toolkit (L18-2, L33-51).
- Treat "not yet visible" and "closed" as different states; the wait must know which one it read.

title: An AT-SPI error name is not proof an object is gone
date: 2026-10-18
category: runtime-errors
module: crates/linux/src/tree/properties/absence.rs, crates/linux/src/tree/resolve/resolve_errors.rs, crates/linux/src/tree/observe/node_evidence.rs, crates/linux/src/tree/resolve/mod.rs, crates/linux/src/tree/properties/toolkit_trust.rs
problem_type: runtime_error
component: atspi-resolver
symptoms:
  - "A live element is reported destroyed because one read returned UnknownObject, UnknownMethod or UnknownInterface."
  - "A destroyed element still resolves because a read of its stored object path succeeded."
  - "An exited application is reported as a destroyed element, or a stopped one as an exited one."
tags: [linux, at-spi, d-bus, stale-ref, resolution, error-names, toolkits]
---

## Problem

Re-identifying a stored ref on Linux needs a verdict on whether the element still exists. The obvious rule reads the stored object path and treats the D-Bus error names `UnknownObject` / `UnknownMethod` as "gone". Measured against live GTK3, GTK4, Qt 6 and Chromium (`probes/linux/FINDINGS.md` L17-1 to L17-12), that rule is wrong in both directions.

## What the toolkits actually do

- **The same names mean "not implemented" on live objects** (L17-2). Qt answers `UnknownObject` to `Text.GetText` on 46 of 48 live nodes and `UnknownInterface` to `Properties.Get` of `Value`; GTK4 answers `UnknownMethod`; GTK3 answers `Failed`. Qt also answers `UnknownInterface` to `Properties.GetAll(Accessible)` on every live node (L17-3), so a `GetAll` failure is no absence signal.
  The same holds on the application interface: GTK3 and Qt refuse `Properties.GetAll(org.a11y.atspi.Application)` while answering `Get(ToolkitName)` and `Get(Version)` (L27-20, L27-32), so `toolkit_trust.rs` reads the toolkit one property at a time and a refused group read leaves nothing to conclude.
- **Bulk reads can crash the bridge.** A later raw Qt probe killed the app with `Properties.GetAll(Accessible)` while individual `Properties.Get` calls and an interface-guarded walk survived (L41-7). The reader therefore uses concurrent individual properties and checks advertised interfaces before optional reads. Earlier refusal results do not make a bulk read safe.
- **Destroyed objects keep answering.** GTK3 and Chromium objects return their old values for about 16 s after destruction, then `UnknownObject` (L17-6 to L17-8). A successful read of a stored path proves nothing in that window. GTK4 and Qt go quiet at once, with `UnknownMethod` and `UnknownObject`/`UnknownInterface` respectively (L17-1, L17-4).
- **A write to a destroyed GTK3 widget answers success** with a zeroed `GetState` and an empty name (L30-2), so a successful write is no more proof of presence than a successful read. `an-atspi-write-that-returns-success-has-not-changed-anything.md` covers the write path.
- **An exited application is a different error.** SIGKILL and clean quit both give `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown` on the call and `NameHasNoOwner` on a bus-daemon query; never `UnknownObject` (L17-9).
- **A call in flight when the app is killed returns `NoReply`, not `ServiceUnknown`**, for the 27 to 45 ms before the next call sees the app gone (L33-12). `NoReply` is not an `AppGone` name, so a root `GetChildren` that straddles a kill is a transient non-verdict: retry it, and let the next read return `ServiceUnknown`.
- **A closed or hidden Qt dialog stays in the tree.** It keeps `ENABLED`, `RESIZABLE` and `SENSITIVE` and loses `SHOWING` and `VISIBLE` (L33-15), so a window list built from the registry reports a window that is gone. Minimized windows are not that shape: GTK 3, GTK 4, Qt and Chromium keep `SHOWING` or gain `ICONIFIED` (L33-55). A window with neither is a husk, and `crates/linux/src/system/window/ghost_window.rs` leaves it out. A state census that filters by flags can hide the husk or hide a real minimized window, so count by the full state set.
- **A timeout carries no D-Bus error name** (L17-10): a stopped process fails every read with a local `TIMED_OUT` after the client limit, and the registry still lists it. Registry presence is no liveness evidence.
- **A hidden GTK4 tab page** leaves the tree while its objects still answer every universal read (L17-5), so a direct-path read can find what a descent cannot.

## Solution

Classify in layers, as `crates/linux/src/tree/properties/absence.rs` does.

1. `Failure` sorts one failed call: `AppGone` (`ServiceUnknown`, `NameHasNoOwner`), `Suspect` (the three names above), `TimedOut`, `Other`. `Suspect` is never a verdict on its own.
2. `Liveness` is read from the node's own `Accessible.GetRole`, which every live node of every toolkit answers (L17-11). A field read that fails as `Suspect` becomes "object gone" only when `GetRole` also fails in the suspect family; otherwise the failure stays on its field (`read_failure`). `GetAll` and `GetChildAtIndex` are not valid corroboration: Qt fails the first and GTK4 childless nodes fail the second.
3. Presence is decided by the parent's child list, not by the object's own reads (L17-12): the resolver follows the stored child-index path down from the verified window frame (`path_descent.rs`), and a landing is accepted only if its evidence still matches the stored identity. A node that merely answers is not a positive. The `Parent` property is never climbed (L2-2).
4. Map to settled answers in `resolve_errors.rs`: an app that left the bus is `STALE_REF` kind `resolve_owning_process_exited` only when `/proc` shows the process gone, and `resolve_owner_unreachable` otherwise (`owner_unreachable`), because a missing bus owner does not prove an exit; a destroyed object is `resolve_target_destroyed`; a full search with no match is `resolve_no_candidate`. After that mapping, `resolve/mod.rs` checks whether `/proc` shows the owning process stopped when the error is a timeout or an incomplete identity observation (`resolution_identity_unknown`). With stopped-process evidence, both become `APP_UNRESPONSIVE` (`stopped_aware`). Without it, a timeout stays unchanged, and an incomplete observation becomes a retryable `STALE_REF`. Other errors pass through.

### Process state needs independent evidence

The lifecycle path in `crates/linux/src/system/process/process_state.rs` asks a different question from element resolution. `system/process/liveness.rs` checks the expected process-instance token against `/proc` before and after the accessibility probes: a missing, zombie, dead or replaced process is `Exited`; an unreadable stat is conservatively alive. `kill(pid, 0)` succeeds on a zombie and cannot replace that check.

`process_state_classify.rs` keeps an answered probe, a timed-out probe and an unavailable probe distinct. A stopped process is `Unresponsive` unless it answered. A live process becomes `Unresponsive` after two consecutive accessibility probes time out (`process_state.rs::observe`); one timeout or unavailable evidence leaves it `Running`. The rule was measured against a blocked main loop and healthy applications under load (ledger L31-17, L31-18), not inferred from registry presence. Returning an error for an unavailable probe would let core mistake uncertainty for exit.

## Prevention

- Do not branch on a D-Bus error name alone; ask what else the same name means on a live object, and measure it per toolkit.
- A read that succeeds against a stored path is not positive evidence of presence. Positive evidence is reaching the node by walking from a verified ancestor.
- Keep "app gone", "object gone", "timed out" and "not found" as separate answers; collapsing them turns a native failure into a confident verdict.
- Probe every toolkit before encoding a rule from one: Qt, GTK3, GTK4 and Chromium disagreed on every name here.

--- title: agent-desktop navTitle: Introduction description: A CLI and C library that lets AI agents read and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. --- agent-desktop reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON. Every element an agent can act on gets a ref. The agent acts on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. It ships as a CLI and as a C library for macOS, Windows, and Linux. ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop # macOS, Windows, and Linux agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop skills get desktop # the guide your agent should load first ``` ## What agent-desktop is and is not - **A tool that agents call.** It is not an agent. The observe, act, and verify loop lives in the calling agent or script. - **No model inside.** It never embeds an LLM, has no GUI, and has no interactive prompt. Every command prints one JSON envelope and exits. - **Desktop apps only.** It does not automate web pages; use [agent-browser](https://agent-browser.dev) for those. For the web contents of a Chromium or Electron app you launch, agent-desktop opens a DevTools port that agent-browser connects to. See [Chromium and Electron apps](/desktop/guides/chromium-and-electron). - **Limited to what apps expose.** It reads accessibility trees and does not match pixels, so it cannot see a UI that publishes no accessibility tree. ## The loop in four commands An agent maps an app, drills into the region it needs, acts on a ref, and checks the result. ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app gnome-calculator --skeleton -i --compact # 1. map: a shallow skeleton agent-desktop snapshot --root @s2txcl95uvubmn:e1 -i --compact # 2. drill: expand one region agent-desktop click @s2txcl95uvubmn:e11 # 3. act: press the 7 button agent-desktop wait --element @s2txcl95uvubmn:e6 --predicate value --value 7 # 4. verify: the display reads 7 ``` Refs carry the id of the snapshot that produced them (`@s2txcl95uvubmn:e11`). [Snapshots and refs](/desktop/snapshots-and-refs) defines them, and [Skeleton and drill-down](/desktop/skeleton-and-drill-down) explains the first two commands. A successful action does not prove the UI changed, so the loop ends with a read. The [quick start](/desktop/quick-start) runs these commands with their output. ## How it works The same chain in text, from the caller to the app: 1. The calling agent: your code or an LLM loop. It runs a command and reads the JSON envelope it prints. 2. The `agent-desktop` CLI, or the [C library](/desktop/ffi) when you call it in process. 3. `agent-desktop-core`: the commands, `RefStore`, and snapshot building. Core defines the `PlatformAdapter` trait and every shared type. 4. `PlatformAdapter`, the only way core reaches an operating system. 5. One platform crate: `agent-desktop-macos`, `agent-desktop-windows`, or `agent-desktop-linux`. 6. The OS accessibility API: the AX API on macOS, UI Automation on Windows, AT-SPI on Linux. 7. The app, which exposes its UI through that API. Core never imports a platform crate, and platform crates never import each other. Only the CLI and the C library connect a platform crate to core, and each picks it at compile time, so a binary drives the OS it was built for. ## Platform support

--- title: C library navTitle: Overview description: Call agent-desktop in process through libagent_desktop_ffi, the C ABI over the same core and platform adapters as the CLI. --- The C library exposes agent-desktop as a shared library: `libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib` on macOS, `libagent_desktop_ffi.so` on Linux, and `agent_desktop_ffi.dll` on Windows. Your program calls `ad_*` functions instead of starting the CLI for each command. Any language with a C FFI can load it; `tests/ffi-python/smoke.py` is the tested reference. The header is `crates/ffi/include/agent_desktop.h`. ## Relationship to the CLI The library and the CLI run the same core and the same platform adapter; the `agent-desktop` binary and the `agent-desktop-ffi` crate are the only two places that connect a platform adapter to core. - **Same envelope.** The command-backed functions return the CLI's JSON envelope as an owned string. See [JSON output](/desktop/json-output). - **Same refs.** `ad_snapshot` writes a refmap under the same [state root](/desktop/configuration#state-root) and returns qualified refs, which `ad_execute_by_ref` resolves strictly. A bare `@e5` returns `AD_RESULT_ERR_INVALID_ARGS`. - **Same safety rules.** Ref actions run the same resolution, actionability checks, and interaction policy as the CLI, and mutations take the same cross-process input lock, so CLI and library calls from one user serialize. - **Same sessions.** `ad_adapter_create_with_session` scopes refmaps to a [session](/desktop/sessions) like `--session`. ## Two layers
LayerFunctionsUse when
JSON entrypointsad_snapshot, ad_execute_by_ref, ad_execute_by_ref_timeout, ad_wait, ad_status, ad_version, ad_trace_show, ad_trace_exportYou run the observe, act, and verify loop: parse the envelope and pass refs back.
Struct-based exact APIsad_list_windows_exact, ad_launch_app_exact, ad_find_exact, ad_get_tree_exact, and the rest of the *_exact family, plus clipboard, mouse, display, notification, and screenshot callsYou need typed results without JSON. These carry process-generation evidence in versioned, size-pinned structs.
## What the library does not expose - `ad_snapshot` always reads the focused window of the app you name. It has no window id, skeleton mode, or `--root` drill-down; use the CLI for those. - `ad_wait` does not expose `wait --event` or `--window-id`. - The library carries no skills. Read the FFI guide with `agent-desktop skills get ffi` from the CLI. ## ABI version `AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR` is 6 in this header. The major increments when a symbol is removed or a struct layout changes; new functions and new result codes are additive. Call `ad_init(AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR)` once after loading the library: a mismatch returns `AD_RESULT_ERR_INVALID_ARGS`, and you should call nothing else. ## Next steps - [Build and link](/desktop/ffi/build-and-link): build the library, link it, and run a minimal program. - [API](/desktop/ffi/api): every function, struct, and enum, grouped by area. - [Ownership, threading, errors](/desktop/ffi/ownership-and-threading): who frees what, which threads may call, and how to read failures.
